workshops.title: Pour one yourself
workshops.description: An afternoon at the studio bench in Surat: you mix the resin, choose the pigments and make the pour. Everything is laid out before you arrive, no experience is needed, and you leave with the piece you made.

image.alt: A long studio table set for eight places, with mixing cups, gloves, pigment jars and empty moulds laid out in a row

printing.title:
From digital form
to physical object.
printing.description: Alongside the pours runs a printer bay — lithophane lamps lit by your photographs, sculptural printed forms, and the filaments and parts that make them.

image.alt: An FDM print head laying translucent blue filament, layer by layer

facts.value: The form is modelled, or your photograph is mapped to depth.
It prints in translucent filament, layer by layer.
Seams are cut back, sanded and finished by hand.

sections.heading: Handcrafted
paragraphs: Every piece passes through human hands.

image.alt: A maker at a lamplit bench, polishing a blue and gold resin vessel with a cloth

sections.heading: Bespoke
paragraphs: Built around your story, not a catalogue.

image.alt: A fresh varmala garland of roses and marigolds beside a pair of shears

sections.heading: Slow made
paragraphs: Time is part of the process, not an obstacle to it.

image.alt: Filled moulds curing overnight under a work lamp

sections.heading: Heirloom
paragraphs: Made to be kept, gifted and passed on.

image.alt: Deep blue resin catching the light across a finished surface
